summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from RIT with a B.E. in Electronics and Telecommunication, and hands-on experience across embedded electronics and firmware on STM32, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi platforms. Background spans bare-metal C firmware, circuit design and schematic generation in EAGLE, and integrating embedded control devices into complete systems from prototype through validation testing.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Organized 10+ exhibitions and technical workshops covering Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept using AI-based real-time chroma keying without a green screen; produced full claims documentation and BOM.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (servo brownout, stale-frame capture, false positives), achieving 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.
Integrated a Jetson and Arduino controller pipeline with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for contact-aware grasping.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
